title: Workforce interactive tool declaration
description: One entry of the project-tools registry (ADR-0027 §3, Epic-025). A tool is declarative: the console renders its form and result from `input`/`output`, and tools-api runs it, so a new tool ships by committing this file plus system.md — no SPA change.

tool_id.description: Immutable id. MUST equal the containing directory name and match the console's TOOL_ID route pattern; it is the last path segment of /projects/{id}/tools/{tool_id} and the EXEC row's skill_name suffix, so renaming it breaks the link to past runs.

summary.description: One line on the tools index card. What the tool does, not how.

version.description: Semver. Recorded on every EXEC row, so a behaviour change (prompt or schema) MUST bump it or the ledger cannot distinguish runs of different tools-in-name-only.

requires.description: Credential types the run resolves from the project. Mirror point of credential-injector.ts:CREDENTIAL_TYPES — see that file's header for the full list of mirrors. A tool that calls the model needs azure.openai.

deployment.description: Azure deployment override. Omit to use the project credential's own deployment, which is the normal case — pinning one here couples the tool to one project's naming.

max_tokens.description: Completion-token cap. Exhausting it THROWS (W-1/W-4), so size it for the largest honest answer: too low turns a good run into a failed one, never into a shorter result.

input.description: JSON Schema for the operator's form. Only a flat object of string/enum/integer fields renders today; the console rejects what it cannot draw rather than dropping fields silently.

output.description: JSON Schema the model is FORCED to answer with, via a single function call with a forced tool_choice (ADR-0027 §5). This is the tool's contract with the renderer.
